newsitem.title: USA: Head of Mexican cartel found guilty on drug charges.
newsitem.headline: Head of Mexican cartel found guilty on drug charges.

text.p: Juan Garcia Abrego, the reputed head of a ruthless Mexican cocaine cartel, was found guilty on Wednesday of charges that he smuggled billions of dollars worth of drugs into the United States.
Garcia Abrego, 52, was convicted on all 22 counts of drug smuggling and money laundering. He faces up to life in prison in what amounts to a major victory for the U.S. government in its war on drugs.

Garcia Abrego sat quietly while the verdict was read but he appeared angry and at one point looked back sternly at his family in the packed federal courtroom in Houston. Family members wept in the hallway moments later.
The eight-man, four-woman jury deliberated for two days before reaching its decision in a trial which began on Sept. 16.

The United States made Garcia Abrego a symbol in the fight against international drug-trafficking when it placed him on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list in March 1995. Drug agents said his Gulf Cartel, operating from northern Mexico, at one time shipped up to a third of cocaine consumed in the United States.
Garcia Abrego was finally captured in January in Monterrey, Mexico, and was quickly deported to Houston for trial.
